text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn will hold consultations today with presidents and parliamentary group leaders of all parliamentary parties to hammer out a governing coalition stance on the possible dispatch of a Hungarian peacekeeping contingent to Albania.
- "I have no intention of amending the income tax and social insurance systems next year", said Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy vowing there will be no "election campaign economic policy" next year.
- President Arpad Goncz left Tuesday for a Latin American tour.
- Judges from the Hague International Court of Justice began a visit to Slovakia Tuesday to observe at first hand various projects connected with the disputed Gabcikovo hydroelectric power plant.
- The State Privatisation and Holding Co. will decide the winner of the privatisation tender for Takarekbank Rt. today.
- Acting on a tip-off, police have prevented the circulation of forged foreign securities worth $60 million.
- Football celebrities will be on hand today for the 70th birthday of Hungary's most famous soccer player Ferenc Puskas at a Hungary vs. Australia friendly in Budapest.
NEPSZABADSAG

- The Coalition Consultative Council, the top decision- making body of the two coalition parties discussed ways for the governing parties to dissociate themselves from political anti-Semitism without jeopardising the operation of Parliament.
- The private Romanian airline DAC Air has set up a direct flight between Budapest and Timisoara, twice a day from April 1.
VILAGGAZDASAG

- The government is scheduled to discuss a proposal for motorway development from 1997 to 2004 at its April 10 session, provided the Ministry of Finance completes a list of major infrastructural development projects targeted for the next four years.

- Hungary has increased its creditworthiness by 4 points over 12 months and 2.9 points over 6 months, the American review Institutional Investor reveals, based on evaluations by the world's largest banks.
- Hungarian Justice and Life Party and the Agricultural Producers' Advocacy Organisation received police permits for staging demonstrations this Friday.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The Defence Ministry and the Manfred Worner Foundation are to jointly stage a military air show in Kecskemet on May 23-25.

- Constantin Dudu Ionescu, state secretary at the Romanian Defence Ministry and Hungarian Defence Ministry deputy state secretary Istvan Gyarmati held talks in Budapest Tuesday on the two countries' NATO integration endeavours and the possible establishment of a joint Hungarian-Romanian contingent for future peace-keeping operations.
- This paper quotes experts claiming that if the grain crop area remains the same size, nothing will save the market from collapse.
NEPSZAVA
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs flew to Cairo on Tuesday for a two-day official visit.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The general assembly of the Budapest Municipal Council on March 27 decided to sell Budapest's fun park, Vidampark Rt.
